title: A link to the past: the Bangia genome connects an ancient body plan to modern stress biology
content: Eukaryotes have occupied Earth for at least 1.65 billion years, as evidenced by some of the oldest unambiguous eukaryotic fossils (Miao et al. 2024). Two endosymbioses were central to this history: an early bacterial union gave rise to mitochondria, while a subsequent association between a mitochondriate eukaryote and a cyanobacterium produced the ancestral plastid (Ochoa de Alda et al. 2014; Martijn et al. 2018). From this photosynthetic ancestor, various lineages emerged, including glaucophytes, red algae, and green plants. Comparing these diverse groups provides the opportunity to investigate the molecular components supporting photosynthetic life and their subsequent diversification in multicellular organisms.
